<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Circle</title>
  <style>
    *,
    *::before,
    *::after {
      box-sizing: border-box;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
    }
    html,
    body {
      height: 100%;
    }
    body {
      display: grid;
      place-items: center;
      background: #f7f7f8;
      overflow: hidden;
    }
    svg {
      width: min(400px, 80vmin);
      height: auto;
      display: block;
    }
    .circle {
      fill: #1f2937;
    }
    @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
      body {
        background: #111827;
      }
      .circle {
        fill: #f9fafb;
      }
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <svg id="ae683f770" viewBox="0 0 400 400" role="img" aria-labelledby="circle-title">
    <title id="circle-title">A solid circle</title>
    <circle class="circle" cx="200" cy="200" r="200"/>
  </svg>
</body>
</html>

content.text:
I updated `0.html` and kept the circle as the single centered element.

What changed:

- **No stray scrollbars.** Replaced the 100vw/100vh sizing, which adds a horizontal scrollbar when a vertical one appears, with a 100% height on html and body.
- **Responsive sizing.** The SVG is now capped at 400px but shrinks on small screens, so the circle is never clipped.
- **Accessibility.** The SVG has an image role, an accessible title, and a descriptive page title instead of the hash.
- **Styling.** Added a universal box-sizing rule, a soft background, an explicit fill color on the circle, and a dark mode variant via prefers-color-scheme.

Open the file in a browser to check it. Resizing the window should keep the circle centered and fully visible.
